description:
FOUND AND FIXED s488b (Opus), as a filler between #1843 and #1841: the script
cache (#1841) is default-ON for `pcl FILE`, and a benched script that ignored
PCL_OPT would have broken the project's own A/B instrument -- so the hole had
to close before the script cache landed.  It was already open for MODULES.

MEASURED FIRST (scratch/s488b/probes/opt-key.pl): one module, one cache dir,
four alternating runs (default, PCL_OPT=none, default, PCL_OPT=none).  Before:
ONE entry, reused by all four.  After: TWO entries, each reused by its own
setting.  The program's OUTPUT is identical in both worlds, which is the point
-- `PCL_OPT=none` is REQUIRED to run identically (Pl/Passes.pm's registry
contract, Pl/t/passes-01.t) -- so this was never a correctness hole.  It is a
MEASUREMENT hole: a warm-cache A/B under PCL_OPT compared the optimized
emission with itself, and the same went for PCL_FACTS and PCL_IR_PLAIN, which
change the emitted TEXT outright.

FIX: the four variables join the COMPILER FINGERPRINT (`p-compiler-stamp`),
which is exactly what that stamp is for -- "what identifies the compiler that
will write this entry" -- so all three caches inherit it at once: the module
cache (the path), the string-eval cache (the stem, since #1843), and the
transpiler's prototype memo.  Unset and empty are ONE answer, since the
compiler reads both as off.

  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp   *p-emission-env-vars*  (a defparameter + a docstring)
  Pl/ProtoCache.pm      our @EMISSION_ENV      (the twin)

THE TWO LISTS ARE COMPARED BY A GATE ROW (Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t), because
nothing else can: one is Lisp and one is Perl, and a variable added to one and
forgotten in the other would make the module cache notice a PCL_OPT change
while the prototype memo did not.

WHAT IS IN THE LIST AND WHY: PCL_OPT and PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT switch named speed
transforms off (Pl/Passes.pm:130-131); PCL_FACTS emits the `p-fact` wrappers
that licensed them (Pl/Passes.pm:113); PCL_IR_PLAIN changes the IR's shape
(Pl/CLForm.pm:325 `ir_plain`).  Variables that only WARN or DUMP are
deliberately out -- PCL_E2_RAW_CENSUS, PCL_V2_SEAM_CENSUS, PCL_DROP_LOG,
PCL_PROTO_ORACLE, PCL_FASL_DEBUG, PCL_PROTO_STATS -- because the emitted text
is what the list is about.  PCL_RAW_ELEMS is a RUNTIME gate (per process, an
init hook), not a transpile input, so it is out too.

`pcl --cache-info` prints an `emission env:` line (either the settings in force
or "none set -- the default emission"), beside the perl binary and PPI lines
#1843 added -- the same diagnostic answering "why did my whole cache
re-transpile" and "why is my A/B flat".

COST: four getenv(3)s per process, inside a stamp that is memoised per process.

Guards: Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t (5 rows: the two --cache-info lines, the stamp
DIFFERING under PCL_OPT, and the two-lists-agree pair), inverse-verified on a
`git archive 11ef34a1` extraction.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111.

Related: #1843 (the fingerprint gained perl + PPI in the same batch), #1119
(the fingerprint itself), #383 (the optimization registry), #1841.
subject: FIXED s488b: the caches did not key on the environment that SELECTS an emission (PCL_OPT / PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT / PCL_FACTS / PCL_IR_PLAIN), so `PCL_OPT=none` on a warm cache silently re-ran the OPTIMIZED transpile -- an A/B measured one side twice, and measurement is Target A's instrument
